chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Stuff Smith's mental breakdown in Moline, and Autrey handling the band's money
summary: In Moline, Illinois, Stuff, drinking rum and Cokes and spending the band's money, lost his mind; Autrey had been put in charge of paying the band by Joe Glaser.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Very, very, very, when -- Moline, Illinois, you know where that is?

You've heard of it. Well I was with -- there with Stuff, and we come out California and Chicago, and that business, and Stuff took ill. He was -- well, I would say that he was -- he lost his mind, or he was losing his mind, or -- I'm trying to think of a nicer way -- you know, I'm trying to think of a nice way to put it. Anyway, --
: Well I mean technically, do you know what was wrong with him at the time? Whether it's nice or

No, no. What I mean is -- I don't like to be -- I had to call the authorities, and they came in the -- picked him up, put handcuffs on him, took him out, because it was about ten below zero, and he had stripped down to his trousers, and he's walking through the --

Yeah, we were in Moline, Illinois. I'm trying to think of the club we were working. And it was a very nice club, too. And I was there -- at that particular time Joe Glaser had booked us in there, and for business reasons Joe had turned everything over to me, and asked me to take charge of the business of collecting the money, paying the band off, including Stuff, and whatnot, because Stuff was such a generous (Laughs) -- he would give the money, my money, anybody else's money, because he was every night, give me a hundred, give me a hundred-fifty, give me two hundred, anyway.

We knew he'd keep that up, you know, and the next night he may say give me three hundred, two hundred, well when payday comes there's nothing left. You know. And he didn't realize it was accounted -- anyway, I had charge of the monies, and so Stuff -- I think that helped to make him feel worse, so -- and he -- one of the night -- that time he was drinking rum and Coke, and he would have quite, quite,
quite a few a night of rum and Cokes, you know?
Could he hold his liquor the way Fats could?

No, never know -- no, he couldn't, but he drank a heck of a lot. But, I had to give it to him, he didn't stagger and fall out and get sick. He just went out of his mind, I guess. I'm going to put it that way. You know? And sweets too, sweet stuff, rum and Coke, I couldn't drink it anyway, the thoughts of it made me sick.
